{{short description|None}}
{{Main article|Tennis at the Summer Olympics}}
[[File:R.F.Doherty Beginning of Low Backhand Drive.jpg|thumb|[[Reginald Doherty]], four-time Olympic medalist]]
[[File:VenusWilliams (cropped).jpg|thumb|[[Venus Williams]], five-time Olympic medalist]]

[[Tennis]] was first contested as a [[Summer Olympic Games|Summer Olympic sport]] in the [[1896 Summer Olympics|1896 Olympic Games]] until [[1924 Summer Olympics|1924]] (excluding 1916 due to [[World War I]]), before going on hiatus due to disputes between the [[International Tennis Federation|International Lawn Tennis Federation]] and the [[International Olympic Committee]] over how to define amateur players.<ref>{{cite web | author=Soltis, Greg | date=July 27, 2012 | url=http://www.livescience.com/2782-olympic-events-history.html | title=Olympic Events Through History | publisher=[[LiveScience]] | access-date=2012-08-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | author=Williams, Wythe | date=July 27, 1928 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1928/07/27/archives/soccer-and-tennis-barred-in-olympics-international-body-by-1614.html | title=SOCCER AND TENNIS BARRED IN OLYMPICS | work=[[The New York Times]] | access-date=2012-08-01}}</ref> After two appearances as a [[demonstration sport]] in [[Tennis at the 1968 Summer Olympics|1968]] and [[Tennis at the 1984 Summer Olympics|1984]] (with a U-21 age limit),<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.itftennis.com/olympics/history/history/overview.aspx | title=Olympic Tennis Event – History: Overview | publisher=[[International Tennis Federation]] | access-date=2012-08-01}}</ref> it was reinstated as a full medal sport in [[1988 Summer Olympics|1988]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1981/10/02/sports/2-more-olympic-games.html | title=2 More Olympic Games | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=October 2, 1981 | access-date=2012-08-01}}</ref>

[[Kathleen McKane Godfree]] (one gold, two silvers, and two bronzes) and [[Venus Williams]] (four gold, one silver) are tied as the record holders for the most Olympic medals in tennis. [[Serena Williams]] and [[Venus Williams]] won a record four gold medals. [[Reginald Doherty]] is the record holder for most medals in men's tennis (three gold and one bronze). [[Andy Murray]] is the only player (male or female) to have won two singles gold medals.

Only on three occasions has a player defended their gold medal: [[Gigi Fernández]] and [[Mary Joe Fernández]] in women's doubles in [[Tennis at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's doubles|1992]] and [[Tennis at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Women's doubles|1996]], [[Serena Williams]] and [[Venus Williams]] in women's doubles in [[Tennis at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's doubles|2008]] and [[Tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's doubles|2012]], and [[Andy Murray]] in the men's singles in [[Tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|2012]] and [[Tennis at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|2016]].
